title: Destroyer returns from 11-month-deployment
zh_title: 驱逐舰结束 11 个月的部署返回
summary: 夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。斯普鲁亚
content:
夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。另一艘阿利伯克级驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号在经过 12 个月的部署后于今天返回家园，驻日本的约翰·芬恩号船员被告知预计将进行 13 至 14 个月的部署。正如《防务一号》10 月 22 日报道的那样，海军官员告诉家属，在可预见的未来，部署时间预计为 10 到 10 个月，这与近几十年来典型的 7 个月部署形成鲜明对比。海军最高军士长、海军军士长约翰·佩里曼 (John Perryman) 一周后证实了这一点，并表示至少在未来几年内，10 至 11 个月将成为常态。迈克尔·墨菲号中校表示，“迈克尔·墨菲”号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开夏威夷，穿过南中国海和马六甲海峡，然后到达北阿拉伯海，并在那里度过了大部分部署时间。大卫·尼古拉斯一个月前接任这艘驱逐舰的指挥。
尼古拉斯说，“迈克尔·墨菲”号在“史诗狂怒”行动期间发动了“战斧”导弹袭击，并参与了霍尔木兹海峡的封锁。“我非常自豪能够成为这个团队的一员，”他说。 “这是我有幸共事过的最有韧性的团队。”尼古拉斯此前指挥过另一艘导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号。据海军新闻稿称，当他于 9 月 10 日将掌权交给继任者时，他将成为罗德岛州水面作战学校的教官。但一名海军官员向《防务一号》证实，当“迈克尔·墨菲”号的前任上司中校改变了他的计划。凯特琳·坎宁安 (Caitlin Cunningham) 在执掌约 11 个月后，因“失去信心”而于 9 月 27 日被解职。在周四的返校节上，三等士官杰西·布莱森第一个下船，成为“初吻”抽奖的获胜者。他和妻子阿里安娜·里奥斯站在一起，开玩笑说这次部署涉及“大量的水”。 “加入海军，看看世界——但世界 70% 都是水，”他笑着说。但是，他补充说，工作人员很棒。 “我认为你可以把这艘船上的任何人放在任何其他船上，他们都会脱颖而出，”布莱森说。 ]]>

【原文 English Original】
PEARL HARBOR, Hawaii —After a 346-day deployment that included operations in the South China Sea, 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz, 43 replenishments at sea and the removal of its commander 10 months in, the guided-missile-destroyer Michael Murphy returned home Thursday, welcomed by hula dancers and a rainbow stretching over the channel. The ship was attached to the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group for much of its deployment, though the aircraft carrier returned to its home in San Diego on Oct. 8. But any deployment-length records it may have broken were short lived. The Spruance, another Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, returned home today after a 12-month deployment, and the Japan-based John Finn crew has been told to expect a 13- to 14-month deployment. As Defense One reported on Oct. 22, Navy officials have told families to expect 10- to 10-month deployments for the foreseeable future—a stark contrast from the typical 7-month deployments of recent decades. The Navy’s top enlisted sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, confirmed that a week later, saying 10-11 months will be the norm for at least a few years. The Micheal Murphy left Hawaii on Dec. 1, 2025, and sailed through the South China Sea and Strait of Malacca before reaching the North Arabian Sea, where it spent the bulk of the deployment, said Cmdr. David Nicolas, who took command of the destroyer a month ago. The Michael Murphy launched Tomahawk missile strikes during Operation Epic Fury and took part in the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Nicolas said. “I’m incredibly proud to be part of this team,” he said. “This is the most resilient crew that I’ve had the pleasure to serve with.” Nicolas previously commanded the Oscar Austin, another guided-missile destroyer. When he handed over the helm to his successor on Sept. 10, he was slated to become an instructor at Surface Warfare Schools in Rhode Island, according to a Navy press release . But a Navy official confirmed to Defense One that his plans were changed when the Michael Murphy’s previous boss, Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham, was relieved on Sept. 27 due to a “loss of confidence” after roughly 11 months in charge.    At Thursday’s homecoming, Petty Officer 3rd Class Jesse Bryson was first off the ship, as the winner of the “first kiss” raffle. Standing with his wife, Arianna Rios, he joked that the deployment involved “a lot of water.” “Join the Navy, see the world—but the world is 70-percent water,” he said with a laugh. But, he added, the crew was great. “I think you could put anyone from this ship on any other ship and they’d stand out,” Bryson said. ]]>

title: ‘Davidson Window’ Admiral Hopes He Was Wrong On China’s Ability To Take Taiwan By 2027
zh_title: “戴维森之窗”海军上将希望他对中国 2027 年占领台湾能力的判断是错误的
summary: 五年前，这位在国会作证的人提出了所谓的“戴维森窗口”，即中国有能力在 2027 年之前对台湾发动可信的入侵，现在这个日期即将到来，他为他的想法提供了一些见解。当时在太平洋地区指挥美军的海军上将菲利普·戴维森 (Philip Davidson) 在周五发布的播客中表示，自他 2021 年退役以来发生的一些事态发展可能会改变他的预测。然而，美国印太司令部（现太平洋司令部或PACOM）前司令告诉我们为什么要关心这个问题
content:
五年前，这位在国会作证的人提出了所谓的“戴维森窗口”，即中国有能力在 2027 年之前对台湾发动可信的入侵，现在这个日期即将到来，他为他的想法提供了一些见解。当时在太平洋地区指挥美军的海军上将菲利普·戴维森 (Philip Davidson) 在周五发布的播客中表示，自他 2021 年退役以来发生的一些事态发展可能会改变他的预测。然而，美国印太司令部（现太平洋司令部或PACOM）前司令告诉《我们为什么要关心印太？》他仍然认为有理由担心。他特别敦促美国在入侵台湾之前向台湾提供军事援助，以更好地威慑中国采取行动。中国军队练习海滩登陆。 (解放军) 戴维森发表上述声明之际，中国一直在稳步增加在台湾周边的军事演习，中国认为台湾是一个分裂的省份，有朝一日将重新置于其控制之下。在了解戴维森对 SeaLight 基金会创始人兼执行董事雷·鲍威尔 (Ray Powell) 和 BowerGroupAsia 高级顾问吉姆·卡鲁索 (Jim Carouso) 所说的话之前，让我们回顾一下戴维森于 2021 年 3 月 9 日对参议院军事委员会所说的话。
戴维森在谈到中国​​时表示：“我担心他们正在加速实现取代美国的野心，以及我们在基于规则的国际秩序中发挥领导作用的野心，他们长期以来一直表示希望在 2050 年之前实现这一目标，我担心他们会进一步接近这一目标。”菲利普·戴维森，当时担任海军上将和美国印度太平洋司令部司令。 （美国海军）两年后，对所谓“戴维森之窗”的评估得到了中央情报局（CIA）的支持。时任中央情报局局长比尔·伯恩斯 (Bill Burns) 表示：“习主席已指示中国军事领导层解放军 (PLA) 在 2027 年之前做好入侵台湾的准备。”从那以后发生了什么变化？ “从本质上讲，我希望自己是错的，”戴维森在谈到他的国会证词时说道。 “如果我错了，那就意味着我们向印太司令部建议的事情、美国政府和其他国家政府在过去七年里采取的事情是有效的。而且没有发生战争。” “我主张，从军事意义上来说，五套能力——我认为很重要的投资指南，”戴维森解释道，他现在是国防承包商 AV 的董事会成员。
“美国需要重新考虑其在印太地区的兵力态势和设计——我们在哪里、我们如何部署、我们轮换什么、这些部队的能力是什么。我们还需要更多样化、更大规模的联合部队火力，这意味着进攻性火力不仅来自海上，还来自陆地和空中。”这位海军上将补充道：“你现在肯定会看到这种情况正在发生，包括部署和导弹部署、海军陆战队、陆军在菲律宾和第一岛链沿线的部署。” “这很有帮助。”第 1 多域特遣部队远程火力营第 3 野战炮兵团第 5 营查理炮台的中程能力 (MRC) 发射器抵达菲律宾吕宋岛北部战区，这是该能力首次部署到战区的一部分

【原文 English Original】
The man whose congressional testimony five years ago led to what’s known as the “Davidson Window” for China being capable of launching a credible invasion of Taiwan by 2027 is offering some insights into what he is thinking now that the date is drawing near. Philip Davidson – the admiral who led U.S. forces in the Pacific at the time – said on a podcast released Friday that several developments have taken place since he retired in 2021 that could change his projection. However, the former commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (now Pacific Command or PACOM) told the Why Should We Care About the Indo-Pacific? podcast he still sees reasons for concern. In particular, he urged the U.S. to deliver military aid to Taiwan before an invasion to better deter China from acting. Chinese forces practice a beach landing. (PLA) Davidson’s statements were delivered as China has been steadily increasing military exercises around Taiwan , which it considers a breakaway province that it will someday bring back under its control. Before getting into what Davidson told podcasters Ray Powell, founder and executive director of the SeaLight Foundation , and Jim Carouso, a senior advisor at BowerGroupAsia , let’s recall what Davidson told the Senate Armed Services Committee on March 9, 2021. “I worry that they are accelerating their ambitions to supplant the United States, and our leadership role in the rules-based international order, which they have long said that they want to do that by 2050, I am worried about them moving that target closer,” Davidson said of China. “Taiwan is clearly one of their ambitions before then, and I think the threat is manifest during this decade, in fact, in the next six years.” Philip Davidson when he was a Navy admiral and commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command. (USN) The assessment of the so-called “Davidson Window” was backed two years later by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). “President Xi has instructed the PLA [People’s Liberation Army], the Chinese military leadership, to be ready by 2027 to invade Taiwan,” then-CIA Director Bill Burns stated . What’s Changed Since Then? “At the heart of it, I’m hoping to be wrong,” said Davidson about his congressional testimony. “If I’m wrong, that means the things we recommended from Indo-Pacific Command, the things that the United States government and other governments have undertaken over the last seven years, have been effective. And there hasn’t been war.” “I advocated for, just in the military sense, five capability sets – investment guidelines that I thought were important to do,” explained Davidson, now on the board of directors at defense contractor AV . “The United States needed to rethink its force posture and design in the region, in the Indo-Pacific – where we are, how we deployed, what we rotated through, what the capabilities of those sets were. We also needed more diverse and a larger set of joint force fires, meaning offensive fires, not just from the sea, but from land and air domain.” “You’re certainly seeing that play out right now, with deployments and missile deployments, with Marine formations , Army formations in the Philippines and along the First Island Chain,” the admiral added. “That has been a help.” Mid-Range Capability (MRC) Launcher from Charlie Battery, 5th Battalion, 3rd Field Artillery Regiment, Long Range Fires Battalion, 1st Multi-Domain Task Force arrives as part of the capability’s first deployment into theater on Northern Luzon, Philippines, April 8, 2024. The MRC deployment aims to enhance Philippine maritime defense capabilities, while bolstering interoperability and readiness within the U.S.-Philippine Alliance. (U.S. Army) U.S. Army In addition, Davidson noted that the U.S. “needed to improve our exercises, our experimentation, and our innovation in the region. We have deepened the relationship with Japan and Australia in the Keen series of exercises over the last five years, and in a way that was kind of unheard of in my day, which I think is a profound improvement.” The Keen Sword training exercise occurred last month and saw about “45,000 Japan Self-Defense Force, 11,000 U.S. service members and forces from Australia, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines…participating alongside observers from the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom,” according to the U.S. Navy. A Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Landing Craft Air Cushion (LCAC) hovercraft assigned to Amphibious Warfare Squadron One, Amphibious and Mine Warfare Group, coasts into the harbor at Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni, Japan, Oct. 28, 2026, during Keen Sword. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Donald Dugger) Lance Cpl. Donald Dugger Japan taking a more assertive security posture toward China has been a huge change from when he was in command, Davidson noted. “Japan absolutely has come forward, they reissued their national security strategy in December of [2022], and there were a number of alliance announcements made in January of [2023],” he explained.  The Japanese doubled their investment in defense from 1% to 2% of its GDP, Davidson highlighted. Japan also “established space [and] cyber forces, instilled the cybersecurity principles and laws that would be necessary to deepen our relationship in a classified way. And this is almost unknown to anybody in America. Completely redistributed and reset their ground formations and air formations in the Southwest Island chain, between Okinawa and along the Ryukyu chain.” “Most importantly, they identified China as the strategic threat in the region,” Davidson proffered. “And in the alliance announcement in January of [2023] with us, said that our interests have converged in this regard.” A Japan Air Self-Defense Force F-15 fighter performs during the Komatsu Air Festival on September 26, 2026 in Komatsu, Japan. (Photo by Zhang Hui/VCG via Getty Images) VCG Taiwan too has made some needed improvements in its approach to defending itself since he retired, Davidson explained. “You have to be encouraged by Taiwan’s actions taken since then,” he stated. “They expanded the conscription timeline from just a few months to a year of service. They have done an enormous amount of work in their national emergency preparedness realm.” Davidson also credited Adm. Lee Hsi-min, chief of the Taiwanese Armed Forces general staff from 2017 to 2019, for developing the Overall Defense Concept (ODC). Lee envisioned a mix of mines, uncrewed aerial systems (UAS), uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs), uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs), crewed coastal defense boats, land-based mobile short- and medium-range precision munitions, precision-guided multiple launch rocket systems, man portable air defense systems (MANPADS), anti-armor rocket systems and electronic warfare measures to counter the PLA’s overwhelming advantages in aviation and naval assets and long-range fires. Taiwan sits about 130 miles east of China. (Google Earth) “He said, ‘We really have to develop the kind of asymmetric capabilities that help round out our lack of capacity vis-a-vis its relationship with the People’s Republic of China, and make sure that we have a strategic and operational design that can kill in the littoral and along the landing beaches and things like that,’” Davidson pointed out. “They’ve been getting after autonomy. They’ve been getting after robotics and drones and sensing.” In 2025, Taiwan revealed a new drone boat, or uncrewed surface vessel (USV), the Endeavor Manta, said to be the first of its kind for the Republic of China Navy (ROCN). However, as we have frequently pointed out , Taiwan is still far behind where it needs to be in many of these areas, but especially uncrewed systems . In addition, Davidson said growing relations with the Philippines and Australia are also helping. Australia signed the Australia–United Kingdom–United States security partnership (AUKUS) in September 2021, months after Davidson retired. AUKUS calls for the United States and Britain to share nuclear-submarine technology with Australia. A rendering of the future SSN-AUKUS design. (U.K. Ministry of Defense) “So over the span of the last six years since March 9 of 2021, you’ve seen a lot of change that I think has reinforced the deterrence of the West here, and I think that’s important to note,” Davidson stated. What Still Needs To Change Despite seeing the U.S. and its allies better prepared to defend against a Chinese invasion of Taiwan, Davidson said he is concerned that the U.S. is not moving fast enough to provide promised military aid. “I would like to see the $14 billion in committed [Foreign Military Sales] to Taiwan move over there in the next few months or a year,” Davidson stated. Approval of the package, which is a major point of controversy with China, has been stalled, Taiwan’s Defense Minister Wellington Koo said in September . The minister’s remarks “come as concerns mount that President Donald Trump could halt arms sales to Taiwan. China has pressed Washington to halt the arms sales, most prominently during a May summit in Beijing between Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping,” The Associated Press noted . “The United States paused the $14 billion arms deal after that meeting.” The package “largely consists of [Patriot] PAC-3 and NASAMS [ National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile System ] air defense missiles,” Reuters reported . However, another huge factor beyond tensions with China is the U.S. supply of these air defense munitions, which has been drastically affected by the current and recent Middle East conflicts . Donations to Ukraine have also eaten into U.S. stocks. The lack of sufficient magazine depth is an issue that TWZ has raised frequently for years, and especially in regard to America’s air and missile defenses , in particular. Commitments for deliveries to 20 other nations and an overall insatiable global demand for interceptors due to numerous destabilizing events has put further strain on the supply of American interceptors. All this is also straining the ability of industry to provide enough capacity. For instance, current PAC-3 MSE production “is around the baseline rate of 650 interceptors per year, with half the deliveries going to the United States and the rest to allies and partners,” according to a report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). The Pentagon is trying to boost production. Under a contract with the Pentagon inked in January , Lockheed Martin is committed to raising annual Patriot output to 2,000 interceptors. A Patriot PAC-3 interceptor (Lockheed Martin) In addition to wanting to see the arms package pushed forward, Davidson warned about China’s information warfare capabilities. “The one thing that has really jumped out at me that was a problem, certainly, when I was the Indo-Pacific commander, but it’s worse now, is the information environment,” Davidson posited. “China is working to undermine the democratic processes in Taiwan. They’re working to undermine any U.S. citizens’ confidence in business leadership and political leadership and military leadership. They’re exploiting accidents or difficulties that someone might be having to flood social networks, and it’s happening not just from China, but from Russia and Iran and independent actors elsewhere. “ “It’s really dangerous,” the former commander emphasized. “There’s been some estimations that some of the activity from bots and from propaganda players is accounting for up to 70% of the commentary in social media threads here and there, and that’s a much more difficult place to be.” Davidson said the U.S. needs to step up its own information warfare capabilities. “I think we should be putting as much effort into [the information domain] as we’ve been putting into drones and autonomy and things like that in this day and age,” Davidson stated. Chinese hovercraft land on a beach during training. (PLAN) Davidson did not address some other glaring issues in regard to China’s potential seizure of Taiwan. The biggest being will the U.S. actually respond militarily if a major Chinese exercise suddenly became an actual invasion operation? Would there even be enough time and what about China’s anti-access capabilities that could keep much of America’s combat power at bay during the early stages of such a conflict? Would there even be support for such an intervention operation domestically, especially considering it could be very bloody and it would surely manifest itself here at home? Then, as we mentioned in the piece, there are many areas where Taiwan seems to be moving far too slowly while China’s military force continues to balloon on nearly all fronts. Regardless, it’s nice to hear from the man who inadvertently gave birth to the “Davidson Window” now that this ominous window of vulnerability he predicted a half decade is cracking open. Contact the author: howard@twz.com The post ‘Davidson Window’ Admiral Hopes He Was Wrong On China’s Ability To Take Taiwan By 2027 appeared first on TWZ .

title: New Bow Sonar Dome For Heavily Damaged Submarine USS Connecticut Seen For The First Time (Updated)
zh_title: 首次出现严重受损的康涅狄格号潜艇的新弓声纳罩（更新）
summary: TWZ 获得了有关海狼级潜艇康涅狄格号在 2021 年在南中国海与水下海山相撞后正在进行维修的新细节。海军一直在考虑大约三年的时间表来建造替换的船首声纳导流罩。最终，仅用了不到一年的时间就建成了。康涅狄格州的总体维修计划已被推迟，我们是第一个报告该船预计要到明年夏天才能恢复使用的人。编者注：这篇报道发表后，Janicki Industries 达成了
content:
TWZ 获得了有关海狼级潜艇康涅狄格号在 2021 年在南中国海与水下海山相撞后正在进行维修的新细节。海军一直在考虑大约三年的时间表来建造替换的船首声纳导流罩。最终，仅用了不到一年的时间就建成了。康涅狄格州的总体维修计划已被推迟，我们是第一个报告该船预计要到明年夏天才能恢复使用的人。编者注：这篇报道发表后，Janicki Industries 联系我们，要求在进行额外审查时删除圆顶的图像。出于礼貌，我们同意了，如果完全获得批准，我们将重新发布它。 Janicki Industries 今天告诉我们，该公司在大约 10 个月内生产出了新型船首声纳导流罩，并于 2024 年交付给海军。据其网站称，Janicki 拥有为美国核潜艇项目生产“声纳罩和精密加工硬件”的历史。它还支持各种备受瞩目的航空航天项目，包括 B-21 袭击者轰炸机和 F-35 联合攻击战斗机。根据一份经过大量编辑的海军事故报告，康涅狄格号的船头在五年前的碰撞事件发生后，最初至少在某种程度上仍然保持着连接状态。然而，当潜艇一瘸一拐地驶向关岛时，整个船首结构随后断裂。
随后，这艘船驶往加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥，然后前往华盛顿州的普吉特海湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施 (PSNS-IMF)，此后一直待在那里。 2023 年，在普吉特湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施中看到的康涅狄格号航空母舰，其船首圆顶明显缺失。美国海军“普吉特海湾海军造船厂和国际货币基金组织（中间维护设施）需要按照船的计划，在其后面没有生产线的情况下安装一个精密的替换圆顶，”贾尼基在撰写本文时还在其网站上表示。 “Janicki 比次佳选择快了 24 个月，因为工作所需的一切都集中在一个屋檐下：适合半球的 5 轴铣床、证明这一点的计量方法以及形成双曲板的 1,000 吨压力机。”本文顶部的部分图片和下面的完整图片显示了 Janicki 专有的五轴铣床在圆顶上工作的情况。海狼级潜艇艏声纳导流罩的尺寸和复杂性怎么强调都不为过。这些船上的船首声纳阵列直径为 24 英尺。圆顶本身的结构必须按照非常严格的规格建造，以使声纳系统正常工作。海狼级潜艇上的艏声纳阵列，其艏穹顶被拆除。公共领域 过去的五角大楼预算文件和国会拨款法案已经强调了更换康涅狄格州弓形声纳罩的预期成本和复杂性。
2021 年，立法者批准了 1000 万美元专门用于圆顶的资金，以及 4000 万美元用于其他“紧急维修”。全部维修费用仍不得而知，但预计将远高于 5000 万美元。 在 2024 年发布的 2025 财年预算提案中，海军还概述了购买额外船首圆顶的计划，以防其任何一艘“海狼”级潜艇再次遭受类似的严重事故。 “海狼级潜艇的保障战略不包括提供替换潜艇

【原文 English Original】
TWZ has obtained new details about the ongoing repairs to the Seawolf class submarine USS Connecticut following collision with an underwater seamount in the South China Sea in 2021. The Navy had been looking at a roughly three-year timeline for the construction of a replacement bow sonar dome. In the end, it took just under a year for it to be built. The overall schedule for repairs to Connecticut has suffered delays, and we were the first to report that the boat is now not expected to return to service until next summer. Editor’s note: After this story was published, Janicki Industries reached out to us to ask that the image of the dome be taken down while an additional review is conducted. Out of courtesy, we agreed, and we will repost it if and when it is fully approved. Janicki Industries produced the new bow sonar dome in approximately 10 months and delivered it to the Navy in 2024, the company told us today. Janicki has a history of producing “sonar domes and precision machined hardware” for U.S. nuclear submarine programs, according to its website . It has also supported various high-profile aerospace programs, including the B-21 Raider bomber and F-35 Joint Strike Fighter . Connecticut ’s bow had initially remained attached, at least to some degree, following the collision five years ago, according to a heavily redacted Navy report on the accident . However, the entire bow structure subsequently broke away as the submarine limped to Guam . The boat then sailed to San Diego, California , and then to the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS-IMF) in Washington State, where it has been ever since. USS Connecticut seen at the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility in 2023 with its bow dome prominently missing. USN “Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & IMF [Intermediate Maintenance Facility] needed a precision replacement dome with no production line behind it, on the boat’s schedule,” Janicki also says on its website at the time of writing . “Janicki delivered it 24 months faster than the next-best option because everything the job needed sits under one roof: 5-axis mills that fit a hemisphere, the metrology to prove it, and the 1,000-ton press that forms double-curved plate.” The picture seen in part at the top of this story and in full below shows one of Janicki’s proprietary five-axis milling machines at work on the dome. The size and complexity of the bow sonar dome on Seawolf class submarines cannot be overstated. The bow sonar arrays on these boats is 24 feet in diameter. The structure of the dome itself has to be built to very exacting specifications for the sonar system to work properly. A look at the bow sonar array on a Seawolf class submarine with its bow dome removed. Public Domain Past Pentagon budget documents and appropriations bills from Congress had already highlighted the expected costs and complexities of replacing Connecticut ’s bow sonar dome. In 2021, lawmakers approved $10 million in funding specifically for the dome, as well as $40 million for other “emergent repairs.” The full repair bill is still unknown, but is expected to be far steeper than just $50 million. In its Fiscal Year 2025 budget proposal , released in 2024, the Navy also outlined plans to acquire an additional bow dome in case any of its Seawolf class submarines suffered another similarly severe mishap. “The Seawolf Class submarines sustainment strategy did not include the provisioning of replacement bow domes; therefore, no replacement bow domes for these in-service submarines are within the Navy’s inventory,” the budget documents explained. “This program would procure one Seawolf Class bow dome for use in the event replacement is required. Funds in FY25 are to purchase a bow dome which has a three plus year lead time.” Note here the mention of a lead time of at least three years, which is in line with Janicki’s statement that the “next-best option” would have taken two years more to do this work. As TWZ has highlighted in years of reporting now, repairs to Connecticut , in general, were always set to be challenging and costly due to the small size of the Seawolf class and the design being long out of production. The Navy originally planned to acquire 29 of these boats, but ultimately bought just three as a result of post-Cold War drawdowns. In addition, shrinking the program of record so severely caused the unit price of each one to rise substantially, just over $10 billion in 2025 dollars. At the time of writing, they are still the most costly attack submarines ever built. The last of the Seawolf class submarines, the highly secretive USS Jimmy Carter , which entered service in 2005, is also a heavily modified sub-type optimized for underwater espionage missions . USS Connecticut at sea in 2009. USN It is also worth noting that the U.S. Navy, as well as some of its foreign counterparts , have repaired similarly severe damage to submarines by cannibalizing entire sections from decommissioned boats in the same class. However, this is not an option given the size of the Seawolf class and the still very high demand for them operationally . The core design offers advanced capabilities that make even USS Seawolf and USS Connecticut especially well suited to a variety of specialized tasks . This is clearly why the Navy has continued to invest so much in returning Connecticut to the fleet. As mentioned, repairs to Connecticut are now not expected to be finished until sometime in the summer of next year. This is the latest in a succession of schedule slips in recent years. The original goal had been for the boat to be back in service by September 2025. “The Navy’s target completion date for the availability is the summer of 2027. PSNS & IMF is dedicated to executing this work with the highest standards of safety, technical accuracy, and craftsmanship to ensure the ship returns to the fleet ready to take its place at the tip of the spear in defense of our nation’s interests,” a Navy official told TWZ in September. “Current work consists of structural and systems restoration and required lifecycle maintenance.” Earlier in the year, the Navy also revealed that it is now planning on sending Connecticut into retirement in 2031. This means the submarine has just four more years of service ahead of it if the current repair schedule holds. The Navy does have plans to acquire a new class of nuclear attack submarines, currently referred to as SSN(X). In the past, the service has described those future boats as more of a direct successor to the Seawolf class than the versions of the Virginia class it is buying now. A picture of the first-in-class USS Seawolf . USN “The analytical conclusion was unequivocal: to dominate high-end peer threats in the middle of this century, a clean sheet design is required. The Virginia class is a fantastic, unmatched world-class warship, and it will remain the backbone of our attack fleet for decades,” Navy Rear Adm. Andrew Miller said at the Naval Submarine League’s main annual conference last week, per USNI News . “As adversary capabilities evolve, we require expanded payload capacity, greater electrical and hydrodynamic margins and unprecedented architectural flexibility that simply cannot be backfitted into an existing hull form.” Miller is currently the head of the Undersea Warfare Division with the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations. In terms of desired key capabilities for SSN(X), the Navy wants “first, higher flank speed and tactical control speed. Two, improved operational availability. Three, decisive lethality. Four, superior stealth and layered survivability, and finally organic robotic and autonomous systems hosting and command and control,” Miller added. “We are redefining the role of the submarine from a standalone hunter-killer to a capital mothership. By launching uncrewed systems directly from submarine torpedo tubes and integrating unmanned [robotic] vehicles into our battle plans, we dramatically expand the tactical reach of our manned fleet.” The first SSN(X) submarines are not expected to begin entering service until the mid-2040s, at the earliest. The Navy will continue acquiring Virginia class submarines in the interim. This includes stretched Block IV and V versions with Virginia Payload Modules (VPM) that will now be categorized as guided-missile types (SSGN). There will also be a one-of-a-kind seabed warfare version of the Virginia , which could well take over for the USS Jimmy Carter. A briefing slide from General Dynamics Electric Boat detailing existing and future planned subvariants of the Virginia class nuclear submarine. The Block VI and V types have now been reclassified as nuclear-powered guided missile submarines (SSGN) rather than nuclear-powered attack submarines (SSN). General Dynamics Electric Boat When it comes to USS Connecticut , if there are no further delays, the fully repaired submarine with its new bow sonar dome should be back in service by the middle of next year. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post New Bow Sonar Dome For Heavily Damaged Submarine USS Connecticut Seen For The First Time (Updated) appeared first on TWZ .

title: Russian Tu-95 Bombers Arrive In Vietnam After Flurry Of Northeast Asia Air Alerts
zh_title: 东北亚空中警报频发后，俄罗斯Tu-95轰炸机抵达越南
summary: 俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动距离中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三边会议仅48小时。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，Tu-95MS 飞行员于 2026 年 1 月 21 日在日本海上空进行了一次飞行。照片由 Russian Defence Min 摄
content:
俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动距离中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三边会议仅48小时。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，2026 年 1 月 21 日，一架 Tu-95MS 的飞行员在前一次飞越日本海时。照片由俄罗斯国防部/阿纳多卢通过 Getty Images 拍摄 Anadolu 11 月 16 日至 17 日，Tu-95MS 轰炸机是几架俄罗斯军用飞机之一，在东北亚进行了广泛的演习，引发了三个地区政府的防空反应。据分析师 AviVector 称，共有五架涡轮螺旋桨动力轰炸机于 11 月 16 日从俄罗斯远东的乌克兰基地起飞。据报道，其中三架轰炸机在三架 Il-78M Midas 空中加油机的支援下，在日本海上空进行了大约 11 小时的训练飞行。据报道，一架 A-50U Mainstay 空中预警和控制飞机也在日本海上空飞行。与此同时，另外两架 Tu-95MS 继续向南驶向越南。今天，乌克兰空军基地的三架 Tu-95MS 和三架 Il-78M 在日本海上空进行了 11 小时的训练飞行。
一架 A-50U（RF-94268，红色 41）从符拉迪沃斯托克机场起飞，在日本海上空进行了一次侦察飞行。两架 Tu-95MS（RF-94202，红色 43；RF-94188，红色 44）… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) 11 月 17 日， 2026 日本和台湾均未正式确定参与各自空域事件的飞机类型。日本防卫省证实，11 月 17 日早些时候，两架据信是俄罗斯的飞机侵犯了福冈县冲之岛西北部的领空。第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分左右进入，于凌晨 4 点 10 分起飞。第二架飞机于凌晨 4 点 09 分左右进入，于 2026 年 4 月 10 日起飞。据日本防卫省称，凌晨 4 点 12 分，日本认为俄罗斯飞机于 11 月 17 日早些时候进入福冈附近冲之岛西北部的日本领空，第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分左右进入日本领空，第二架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分左右进入日本… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — 台湾安全监察站 (@TaiwanMonitor) 2026 年 11 月 17 日，日本防卫省称，日本航空自卫队 (JASDF) 紧急出动西方防空部队的战斗机，发出警告并采取其他措施。
穿过对马海峡后，飞机在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后继续进入太平洋。 2026年11月17日，推测的俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本联合参谋部 该航线使飞机经过连接日本海、东海和西太平洋的几个具有重要战略意义的海上通道。据报道，俄罗斯飞机随后进入韩国防空识别区（KADIZ）。不过，据韩国国防部称，此次事件并未侵犯韩国领空。

【原文 English Original】
Russia has sent a pair of Tu-95MS Bear bombers for a rare visit to Vietnam. Unusually, the aircraft appear to have briefly intruded into Japanese airspace and passed through Taiwan’s Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ) along the way. The activity unfolded just 48 hours before Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S. President Donald Trump are due to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China. A screen grab from a video shows the pilot of a Tu-95MS during a previous flight over the Sea of Japan on January 21, 2026. Photo by Russian Defense Ministry/Anadolu via Getty Images Anadolu The Tu-95MS bombers were among several Russian military aircraft conducting extensive maneuvers across Northeast Asia on November 16-17, prompting air defense responses from three regional governments. According to analyst AviVector , a total of five of the turboprop-powered bombers departed their home base of Ukrainka in Russia’s Far East on November 16. Three of the bombers reportedly conducted an approximately 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan, supported by three Il-78M Midas aerial refueling tankers. An A-50U Mainstay airborne early warning and control aircraft was also reported operating over the Sea of Japan. Meanwhile, the other two Tu-95MS continued south towards Vietnam. Today, three Tu-95MS and three Il-78M from Ukrainka Air Base conducted an 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan. An A-50U (RF-94268, 41 Red) from Vladivostok Airport conducted a reconnaissance flight over the Sea of Japan. Two Tu-95MS (RF-94202, 43 Red; RF-94188, 44… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) November 17, 2026 Neither Japan nor Taiwan officially identified the aircraft types involved in their respective airspace incidents. Japan’s Ministry of Defense confirmed that two separate aircraft believed to be Russian violated its territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, in Fukuoka Prefecture, early on November 17. The first aircraft entered at approximately 4:07 a.m. local time and departed at 4:10 a.m. A second aircraft entered at approximately 4:09 a.m. and departed at 4:12 a.m. Two aircraft Japan believes are Russian entered Japanese territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, off Fukuoka, early Nov. 17, per Japan's Ministry of Defense. The first was inside from about 4:07 to 4:10 a.m. local time and the second from about 4:09 to 4:12 a.m. The Japan… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — Taiwan Security Monitor (台灣安全觀測站) (@TaiwanMonitor) November 17, 2026 The Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) scrambled fighters from its Western Air Defense Force to issue warnings and take other measures, according to the country’s Ministry of Defense. Tokyo subsequently lodged what it described as a strong protest with Moscow over the incident. Japan also provided details of the aircraft’s subsequent route. After passing through the Tsushima Strait , the planes flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan before continuing into the Pacific Ocean. Flight path of the presumed Russian aircraft on November 17, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office The route placed the aircraft through several strategically important maritime approaches connecting the Sea of Japan , East China Sea , and western Pacific. The Russian aircraft then reportedly entered South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ). However, there was no violation of South Korean airspace, according to the South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff. Finally, Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense reported detecting two Russian military aircraft entering its ADIZ from the northeast. Overall, 2 sorties of Russian military aircraft were detected early this morning. The aircraft entered #Taiwan 's ADIZ from the northeast, flew through airspace east of Taiwan, and exited the ADIZ south of Taitung. The #ROCArmedForces have monitored the situation and responded… — 國防部 Ministry of National Defense, ROC(Taiwan) (@MoNDefense) November 17, 2026 The aircraft proceeded through airspace east of Taiwan before exiting south of Taitung. Taiwan’s armed forces monitored the activity and responded accordingly, the Ministry of National Defense said. The incident is notable because Taiwan’s defence ministry publicly identified the aircraft as Russian, rather than simply reporting unidentified military aircraft activity. As we have reported in the past , Chinese aircraft commonly fly into the southwestern part of Taiwan’s ADIZ. It is, however, worth noting that the ADIZ declared by Taiwan covers not only the entirety of the Strait but also portions of mainland China. In terms of Russian aircraft operating in Taiwan’s ADIZ, there are historical precedents, but such activity has been greatly reduced since the end of the Cold War. Taiwanese military analyst Chieh Chung told Focus Taiwan that Soviet and Russian military aircraft had previously operated inside Taiwan’s ADIZ in 1986 and January 2010. "The incident was not the first time Russian or former Soviet military aircraft had entered Taiwan's ADIZ, although such flights have become much less frequent since the end of the Cold War." https://t.co/TPUJL9hfp1 https://t.co/SDB6p3E3pD — Bryce C. Barros 白若詩 (@barros_bryce) November 17, 2026 The two remaining Tu-95MS aircraft continued south towards Vietnam and were subsequently reported at Da Nang on November 17. They were accompanied by a pair of Il-76MD Candid transports, one of which was a modernized -90A variant , to support the deployment. Tu-95MS strategic missile carriers RF-94202, RF-94188. Il-76MD, Da Nang Airport / "Danang 35K Feet". pic.twitter.com/22DaoD8PLP — Massimo Frantarelli (@MrFrantarelli) November 17, 2026 [Russie Vietnam] 2 Tu-95MS des forces aérospatiales russes sont arrivés à l'aéroport international de Da Nang (DAD/VVDN), au Vietnam. 2 avions de transport militaire IL-76 (MD et MD-90A) les accompagnaient. (c) AviaNews pic.twitter.com/4bWfFXFOik — La souris (@La_souris_DA) November 17, 2026 The flights took place against the backdrop of preparations for the November 19 meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin in China. The summit is set to be held on the sidelines of meetings of the  Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), which kick off tomorrow. Putin arrived in Shenzhen today. Trump has traveled first to the Philippines as part of a short tour of Asia before heading to China. Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen in the early hours of Nov. 18 to attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. ： @PDChina pic.twitter.com/5YotpjYY6R — Shenzhen Daily (@szdaily1) November 17, 2026 The proximity of the Russian operation to the Shenzhen meeting raises questions about the strategic signaling of the Russian flights, particularly as the three governments prepare to discuss nuclear arms control, regional security, and other major international issues. The meeting is particularly unusual given the different priorities each leader is bringing to the table . Trump has indicated that he wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals and addressing the war in Iran. The expiration of the New START treaty in February 2026 removed the remaining bilateral limits on U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear forces, adding urgency to the question of future arms-control arrangements. U.S. President Barack Obama, at left, and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, at right, shake hands after signing the New START treaty in 2010. Government of Russia Washington has tempered expectations of an immediate agreement, describing the gathering as an initial opportunity for the three nuclear powers to begin a conversation. Putin, meanwhile, is expected to seek discussion of Russia’s war against Ukraine and the possibility of a negotiated settlement. Moscow has signalled that Ukraine will remain a priority in its discussions with Washington. Beijing’s position is more cautious. China has resisted joining trilateral nuclear arms-control negotiations at this stage, arguing that its nuclear arsenal remains substantially smaller than those of the United States and Russia. Xi is also seeking to present China as a central diplomatic actor capable of facilitating dialogue between the other two powers. An apparent new field of Chinese intercontinental ballistic missile silos identified by Matt Korda and Hans Kristensen from the Federation of American Scientists (FAS) and located near the city of Hami in the eastern end of Xinjiang province, in the northwest of China. Kristensen/Korda/FAS 2021 The timing of the Russian aviation activity is therefore difficult to ignore. The operation demonstrated the geographic reach of Russian long-range aviation, with aircraft moving from Russia’s Far East through the approaches to Japan and Taiwan before continuing towards Vietnam. The Southeast Asian nation was a regular late Cold War operating location for Soviet naval Tu-95 Bear reconnaissance aircraft. Of course, as well as strategic signalling, flights of this kind provide valuable long-range training and intelligence collection, including assessment of regional air defense responses. The November 19 meeting may not produce an agreement on nuclear weapons or other major disputes. Still, the Russian flights underscore the fact that strategic stability in the Indo-Pacific also involves the security concerns of the regional states operating along the approaches to the western Pacific. title: Finland’s Iceye bids €2 billion for Italian rocket maker Avio
zh_title: 芬兰Iceye出价20亿欧元收购意大利火箭制造商Avio
summary: 罗马——芬兰运营商 Iceye 向意大利火箭制造商 Avio 提出了 20 亿欧元现金报价（合 22 亿美元），该报价将整合欧洲的太空能力，并让 Iceye 负责 Avio 向美国导弹业务的扩张。拟议的交易符合减少对外部供应商的依赖并缩小与美国和中国行业领导者之间日益扩大的差距的努力。 “欧洲对主权太空和国防能力的需求正在增长。满足这一需求的工业能力建设需要数年时间，这使得现在投资至关重要，”Iceye 周二表示。菲
content:
罗马——芬兰运营商 Iceye 向意大利火箭制造商 Avio 提出了 20 亿欧元现金报价（合 22 亿美元），该报价将整合欧洲的太空能力，并让 Iceye 负责 Avio 向美国导弹业务的扩张。拟议的交易符合减少对外部供应商的依赖并缩小与美国和中国行业领导者之间日益扩大的差距的努力。 “欧洲对主权太空和国防能力的需求正在增长。满足这一需求的工业能力建设需要数年时间，这使得现在投资至关重要，”Iceye 周二表示。该公司表示，将在五年内向意大利 Avio 投资 10 亿欧元，以扩大 Avio Vega 火箭的客户群。芬兰政府支持这一提议，芬兰国防部长安蒂·哈卡宁表示，“如果完成……将创建一个全球航天工业参与者，通过它，芬兰和整个欧洲国防的自给自足的供应安全将上升到一个新的水平。” Avio 周二表示正在考虑这一收购要约，而拥有 Avio 18% 股份的意大利国家控股国防集团 Leonardo 的首席执行官表示，他对这一收购要约感到“惊喜”，并将予以考虑。 Avio 董事会于周二举行了第一次会议，并表示已开始评估此次出价，Iceye 表示，该出价较该意大利集团周一收盘价溢价 21.3%，较其三个月成交量加权平均价溢价 34.8%。
除了欧洲航天发射活动外，Avio 也是导弹固体火箭发动机的市场领导者。9 月，该公司在弗吉尼亚州赫特的美国新设施破土动工，以实现为美国导弹生产带来急需的额外产能的雄心。 Avio 已与雷神公司合作生产 Mk 104 双推力火箭发动机，并与洛克希德·马丁公司合作在 Hurt 为洛克希德的增程 GMLRS (ER GMLRS) 和精确打击导弹 (PrSM) 项目生产发动机。 Avio 发言人告诉《防务新闻》，如果 Iceye 收购，则需要美国政府的批准以及意大利政府的批准。 9月，Avio宣布9个月的订单额为2.37亿欧元，其中一半与国防相关，其余主要与其Vega C和Vega E发射器有关。 Iceye 表示，其每股 41 欧元的报价将通过全资意大利子公司 Iris 2 发起，目的是使该公司退市。消息传出后，Avio 股价上涨超过 15%，至 39.5 欧元左右。 Iceye 自 2022 年以来一直向乌克兰提供卫星雷达图像，上个月与诺基亚和乌克兰国防部签署了一份意向书，探讨太空合作，包括主权卫星通信。
Iceye首席执行官拉法尔·莫德热夫斯基(Rafal Modrzewski)在赫尔辛基的一次活动上发表讲话时表示，该公司在发起竞标之前已与包括政府在内的相关各方进行了磋商，并且还需要几个月的时间才能完成交易。“这是一次非凡的能力组合……遵循相当明确的行业趋势，带来了全面的垂直整合，”莫德热夫斯基表示，并补充说这对两家公司都有利。材料来自路透社，作者 Giulia Segreti 和 Essi Lehto。

【原文 English Original】
ROME — Finnish operator Iceye has a made €2 billion cash offer ($2.2 billion) for Italian rocket maker Avio which would integrate Europe’s space capabilities as well as putting Iceye in charge of Avio’s expansion into the U.S. missile business. The proposed deal fits with efforts to reduce reliance on external providers and narrow a widening gap with industry leaders in the U.S. and China. “Europe’s need for sovereign space and defense capabilities is growing. Building the industrial capacity to meet that demand takes years, which makes it critical to invest now,” said Iceye on Tuesday. The firm said it would invest €1 billion in Avio in Italy over five years in a bid to expand the customer base of Avio’s Vega rocket. The Finnish government backed the offer, with Finnish Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen stating, “If completed … a global space industry player will be created, through which the self-sufficient security of supply of Finland’s and all of Europe’s defense will rise to a new level.” Avio said on Tuesday it was considering the offer, while the CEO of Italian state controlled defense group Leonardo, which owns an 18% percent stake in Avio, said he was “pleasantly surprised” by the bid and would consider it. Avio’s board held a first meeting on Tuesday and said it had started assessing the bid, which Iceye said offered a 21.3% premium to the Italian group’s closing price on Monday or a 34.8% premium to its three-month volume-weighted average price. Apart from its European space launch activity, Avio is also a market leader in solid rocket motors for missiles. In September it broke ground in Hurt, Virginia, on a new U..S facility to fulfill an ambition to bring much needed extra capacity to U.S. missile production. Avio has already partnered with Raytheon on production of the Mk 104 dual-thrust rocket motor and has teamed with Lockheed Martin to produce motors at Hurt for Lockheed’s Extended Range GMLRS (ER GMLRS) and Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) programs. An Avio spokesman told Defense News that U.S. government approval would be required in the event of a takeover by Iceye, as well as Italian government approval. In September, Avio announced a nine month order intake of €237 million, of which half was defense related, with the remainder mainly related to its Vega C and Vega E launchers. Iceye said its €41-per-share offer will be launched through wholly owned Italian subsidiary Iris 2 with the aim of delisting the company. Avio shares climbed more than 15% to around €39.5 on the news. Iceye has supplied Ukraine with satellite radar imagery since 2022, and last month signed a letter of intent with Nokia and Ukraine’s Defence Ministry to explore cooperation in space, including sovereign satellite communications. Speaking at an event in Helsinki, Iceye CEO Rafal Modrzewski said the company had held consultations with the parties involved, including governments, before launching the bid, and that it would take a few more months to close the transaction. “It’s a phenomenal combination of capabilities … bringing a full vertical integration, following quite clear industry trends,” Modrzewski said, adding that it would be beneficial for both companies. With material from Reuters by Giulia Segreti and Essi Lehto.

由于英伟达丑闻有可能在特朗普与习近平的会谈中重新引发贸易紧张局势，北京仍然持有稀土
随着第三十三次亚太经合组织（APEC）领导人会议本周在深圳开幕，中国制定了广泛的议程，包括推动亚太地区自由贸易路线图。虽然许多人都在关注中国国家主席习近平、美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京本周四举行的最后一刻三边会议，但特朗普和习近平今年的第三次单独双边会谈将把经济问题带到人们的面前。上周爆发的英伟达丑闻加剧了紧张局势，而在华盛顿和北京都有理由维持 2025 年 10 月达成的休战协议之际，半导体出口管制也给贸易谈判带来了阴影。
美国先进半导体走私到中国，以及中国企业远程获取海外计算能力，长期以来一直令华盛顿担忧。 Nvidia-Megaspeed 争议中，一家新加坡云提供商因涉嫌将受限制的芯片转移到中国而受到调查，这进一步暴露了美国出口管制制度的潜在漏洞。 Megaspeed 否认有不当行为。这一事件引发了人们的疑问：出口管制是否能有效遏制中国的技术进步，以及美国如何堵住现有的漏洞。中美贸易往往一次形成一项经济限制和一项技术标准。从境外投资审查到各种实体清单和其他贸易限制，尽管贸易休战，双方都没有停止引入新的限制，而中国 2025 年 4 月的稀土出口许可要求仍然有效。
据报道，Megaspeed 前高管与英伟达 (Nvidia) 黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 有联系，针对其的中国间谍指控已经为国会和商务部提供了新的动力，以加强对半导体的控制。针对黄仁勋辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，中国问题特别委员会主席众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔（John Moolenaar）呼吁国会“迅速采取行动，在年底国防法案中通过两党出口管制立法”。目前的立法工作包括《人工智能监督法案》、《芯片安全法案》和《匹配法案》，其中提出了诸如芯片位置验证要求和半导体制造设备联合控制协调等措施。周末，商务部发布了一项临时最终规则，以解决远程访问计算能力的问题，尽管目前尚不清楚该规则将如何实施和执行。美国对先进芯片的更严格限制可能会招致北京方面通过加强稀土管制或恢复更广泛的限制来进行报复，中国最近将这些限制延长至 2027 年 1 月 10 日。
2025年4月，中国商务部、海关总署发布2025年第18号公告，对7种稀土元素实施出口管制。虽然没有明确针对美国，但中国在关键矿产供应链的主导地位在贸易战升级期间受到了严重影响。这些出口管制扰乱了供应链

As the Nvidia scandal threatens to reignite trade tensions at Trump-Xi talks, Beijing still holds the rare earths - Atlantic Council
China Economy & Business Macroeconomics Trade and tariffs United States and Canada
As the Nvidia scandal threatens to reignite trade tensions at Trump-Xi talks, Beijing still holds the rare earths
As the thirty-third Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting begins this week in Shenzhen, China has set an expansive agenda, including pushing for a roadmap for Asia-Pacific-wide free trade. While many eyes are on the last-minute trilateral meeting among Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin this Thursday, the separate Trump and Xi bilateral, their third this year, will bring economic issues to the fore. The Nvidia scandal that broke last week has added to tensions, and semiconductor export controls loom over the trade negotiations at a moment when both Washington and Beijing have reason to preserve the truce struck in October 2025.
The smuggling of advanced US semiconductors into China, along with Chinese firms’ remote access to computing power abroad, have long concerned Washington. The Nvidia-Megaspeed controversy, in which a Singapore-based cloud provider is under investigation for allegedly diverting restricted chips to China, has further exposed potential gaps in the US export-control regime. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing. The incident has raised questions as to whether export controls are effective in containing Chinese technological advancement and how the US can close existing loopholes. US-China trade is often shaped one economic restriction and one technical standard at a time. From outbound investment screening to various entity lists and other trade restrictions, neither side has ceased introducing new restrictions despite the trade truce, and all the while China’s April 2025 rare earth export licensing requirements remain in force.
The Chinese espionage allegations surrounding a former Megaspeed executive with reported ties to Nvidia’s Jensen Huang have already given Congress and the Department of Commerce new fuel to pursue stronger semiconductor controls. In response to Huang’s resignation as CEO of Nvidia, Representative John Moolenaar, chairman of the Select Committee on China, called on Congress to “act quickly to pass bipartisan export control legislation in the year-end national defense bill.” Current legislative efforts include the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, and the MATCH Act, which propose measures such as requirements for chip-location verification and alignment of allied controls on semiconductor manufacturing equipment. And over the weekend, Commerce released an interim final rule to address remote access to computing power—though it is still unclear how this rule will be implemented and enforced. Tighter US restrictions on advanced chips could invite Beijing’s retaliation through stronger rare earth controls or the reinstatement of the broader restrictions whose suspension China recently extended through January 10, 2027.
In April 2025, China’s Ministry of Commerce and General Administration of Customs issued Announcement No. 18 of 2025, which implemented export controls on seven rare earth elements. While not explicitly targeted at the United States, China’s dominance of critical mineral supply chains was heavily leveraged during the trade war escalation. These export controls disrupted supply chains globally, from automakers to electronics manufacturers. As part of the Busan trade truce, the White House announced that US companies would be provided with a general license for these and other elements, describing it as a “de facto removal of controls China imposed since 2023,” but China did not make a reciprocal announcement guaranteeing access.
As shown in the chart above, US imports of selected controlled rare earth elements from China have not returned to pre–trade war levels, and US manufacturers continue to grapple with shortages of materials necessary for semiconductor production, automobiles, and national defense. International companies, including US firms, have expressed frustration over the Byzantine licensing regime, which requires extensive reporting on supply chains, while shipments remain limited even when licenses are approved.
If the US Congress capitalizes on the momentum from Nvidia’s shakeup, more semiconductor legislation could trigger tighter rare earth controls from China. Beijing could counter by reinstating its currently suspended October 2025 regulations, which would restrict transfers of Chinese-made rare-earth refining equipment and extend export controls to foreign-made products containing Chinese-origin rare earths. And despite new investments in domestic and allied critical mineral supply chains, the United States is not yet better equipped to deal with the implementation of these controls, as alternative mining and refining projects are years away from production.
The realities of long-term strategic competition could expose the limits of Trump’s personal diplomacy with Beijing and potentially jeopardize cooperation through initiatives such as the AI Safety Dialogue or the Board of Trade. China could link progress in these forums to concessions on semiconductor controls, for instance. The fallout from Nvidia is galvanizing Congress and other US agencies to intensify oversight of trade and investment with China in the next few months, and Washington will have to consider how far it can push when faced with Beijing’s rare earths chokehold.
Both Trump and Xi have reason to preserve steady relations ahead of the December Group of Twenty (G20) Leaders’ Summit in Florida, where these conversations will continue, and through the trade truce’s January expiration. But instead of tariffs and trade agreements, export controls could become the major point of contention in negotiations in 2027. While the United States cannot fully diversify its rare earth supply or rebuild a stockpile overnight, China has used its rare earth export controls since April to squeeze companies in Japan, South Korea, and the European Union as well. Diversifying supply will take long-term planning and investment. But as trade negotiations continue, Washington would benefit from a coordinated response to China’s licensing regime and its broader nonmarket practices.
Jessie Yin is an associate director at the Atlantic Council’s GeoEconomics Center.

title: The United States’ Participation in the 2026 East Asia Summit
zh_title: 美国参加2026年东亚峰会
summary: 发言人办公室 美国参加2026年东亚峰会情况介绍 2026年11月18日 在11月17日于菲律宾马尼拉举行的东亚峰会上，美国重申对自由开放印太的承诺，表示支持东盟中心地位，并强调美国是该地区首选的能源和技术伙伴。为在美国与东盟建立关系50周年之前推进全面战略伙伴关系，美国和东盟通过了《落实美国-东盟领导人共识的全面工作计划》
content:
发言人办公室 美国参加2026年东亚峰会情况介绍 2026年11月18日 在11月17日于菲律宾马尼拉举行的东亚峰会上，美国重申对自由开放印太的承诺，表示支持东盟中心地位，并强调美国是该地区首选的能源和技术伙伴。为了在美国-东盟关系成立50周年之前推进全面战略伙伴关系，美国和东盟通过了《实施美国-东盟领导人共同愿景声明的综合工作计划，以促进东盟和美国更强大、更安全和更繁荣》（2026-2030年）。美国强调其与盟友和伙伴一道致力于加强威慑，以维护印太地区的和平与稳定。在两国建交80周年之际，美国祝贺菲律宾成功担任东盟轮值主席国。促进和平，加强自由开放的印太地区 美国将继续在印太地区发挥领导作用，并威慑该地区任何试图通过武力解决争端的国家，这体现了特朗普总统通过实力实现和平的承诺。
美国将继续维护《联合国海洋法公约》所反映的国际法规定的所有国家行使航行和飞越自由的权利，包括在南中国海。台海的和平与稳定对于印太地区的安全与繁荣仍然至关重要，美国反对任何单方面改变现状的行为。美国仍然致力于实现朝鲜完全无核化，并全面执行联合国安理会所有涉朝决议。扩大贸易、能源和技术联系美国仍然是东盟最大的单一国家外国直接投资者，截至 2025 年，该地区的外国直接投资超过 5,570 亿美元，为美国提供了约 532,000 个就业岗位。美国祝贺东盟领导人签署《数字经济框架协议》，该协议有可能为美国科技公司提供更大的机会，让该地区的数字经济到2030年将达到2万亿美元。随着美国超级智能（SI）技术在全球树立黄金标准，美国正在与东南亚伙伴合作，扩大获得美国技术的机会，包括通过美国-东盟SI SPARK计划，这将有助于释放该地区的经济潜力。

【原文 English Original】
Office of the Spokesman The United States’ Participation in the 2026 East Asia Summit Fact Sheet November 18, 2026 At the East Asia Summit in Manila, Philippines on November 17, the United States reaffirmed its commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific, expressed support for ASEAN centrality, and underscored the United States as the region’s preferred partner for energy and technology. To advance their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership ahead of the 50 th anniversary of U.S.-ASEAN relations, the United States and ASEAN adopted the Comprehensive Work Plan to Implement the U.S.-ASEAN Leaders’ Joint Vision Statement to Promote a Stronger, Safer, and More Prosperous ASEAN and America (2026-2030). The United States highlighted its commitment, with allies and partners, to strengthen deterrence to safeguard peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region. The United States congratulated the Philippines on a successful ASEAN chair year, as the two countries mark 80 years of diplomatic relations. Promoting Peace and Strengthening a Free and Open Indo-Pacific Reflecting President Trump’s commitment to peace through strength, the United States will continue to lead in the Indo-Pacific and deter any nation in the region tempted to settle disputes by force. The United States will continue to uphold the right of all nations under international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Seas (UNCLOS) to exercise freedom of navigation and overflight, including in the South China Sea. Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait remain essential to the security and prosperity of the Indo-Pacific and the United States opposes any unilateral change to the status quo. The United States remains committed to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and the full implementation of all DPRK-related UN Security Council resolutions. Expanding Trade, Energy, and Technology Ties The United States remains ASEAN’s largest single country foreign direct investor, with more than $557 billion in foreign direct investment in the region as of 2025, which supports an estimated 532,000 American jobs. The United States congratulated ASEAN leaders for signing the Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which has the potential to provide U.S. technology companies with greater opportunities in the region’s digital economy projected to reach $2 trillion by 2030. As American Super Intelligence (SI) technology sets the gold standard worldwide, the United States is working with Southeast Asian partners to expand access to U.S. technology, including through the U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK program, which will help unlock the region’s economic potential. By signing the AI Opportunity Statement, Vietnam and Cambodia joined other nations in committing to fostering innovation anchored in trusted partnerships. To support the region’s SI readiness, the United States will collaborate with the Government of Indonesia, ASEAN Secretariat, and Carnegie Mellon University to host ASEAN SI Week in Jakarta in December. The United States and the Philippines signed a five-year Economic Prosperity and Resilience Strategic Objective Agreement, which will mobilize investment in critical infrastructure, including in the Luzon Economic Corridor, and secure supply chains with reliable partners. As one of the world’s largest energy producers, the United States can power Southeast Asia’s growth for generations. The United States is ready to work with ASEAN to strengthen the region’s energy security through support for the ASEAN Power Grid. The United States is sharing its 70 years of experience and leadership in nuclear energy by promoting nuclear safety, security, and nonproliferation in Southeast Asia. Building on our existing 123 Agreements with Indonesia and Vietnam, the United States has entered into 123 Agreements with the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand, and launched negotiations with Malaysia. This cooperation will help the region meet its growing energy demand, including reliable power for SI. The United States is expanding civil nuclear cooperation in Southeast Asia, where energy demand is anticipated to triple by 2050. Consistent with the U.S.-Japan-South Korea Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) on Small Modular Reactor (SMR) deployments, the United States is providing SMR control room simulators and other technical assistance to Indonesia under the Department’s Foundational Infrastructure for the Responsible Use of Small Modular Reactor Technology (FIRST) program to help establish Indonesia as a regional SMR hub. These partnerships strengthen energy security, drive economic growth, and support jobs in the United States and across the region. Combating Scams and Transnational Crime Scam groups based in Southeast Asia stole at least $18.2 billion from Americans and around $23 billion from citizens of ASEAN member states in 2025. In response, President Trump issued Executive Order 14390, titled “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” and the Department of State has confronted these criminal groups head on. The Department is directing an additional $26.2 million to train and equip Southeast Asian law enforcement and criminal justice officials to work with U.S. law enforcement to catch and prosecute scam network operators. The United States and 12 regional partners in the Contact Group to Counter Criminal Online Scams agreed to a Statement of Principles to drive joint action to dismantle the scam syndicates targeting our people. The United States and ASEAN also adopted the U.S.-ASEAN Statement on 10 Public-Private Partnership Principles for Tackling Online Scams, deepening regional and private-sector cooperation.

title: US surges power projection to westernmost island chain as Russia, China loom
zh_title: 随着俄罗斯和中国的逼近，美国加大了向最西端岛链的兵力投射
summary: 美国空军正在加强在该国最西端岛屿的训练，寻求开发更多的地方来投射力量并监视太平洋和北极的对手。这些努力在十月下旬就可见一斑，当时空军部署到阿拉斯加阿留申群岛的谢米亚岛进行一次罕见的演习，空军发布了一份概述其在关岛附近岛屿行动计划的提案。在比阿拉斯加大陆更靠近俄罗斯的谢米亚，10 月 18 日至 26 日期间，F-16、加油机和货机部署到埃尔克森机场。
content:
美国空军正在加强在该国最西端岛屿的训练，寻求开发更多的地方来投射力量并监视太平洋和北极的对手。这些努力在十月下旬就可见一斑，当时空军部署到阿拉斯加阿留申群岛的谢米亚岛进行一次罕见的演习，空军发布了一份概述其在关岛附近岛屿行动计划的提案。谢米亚距离俄罗斯比阿拉斯加大陆更近，10 月 18 日至 26 日期间，F-16、加油机和货机部署到厄里克森机场。在那里，这些喷气式飞机“保持警惕”，机组人员就位，随时准备在接到通知后立即起飞。阿拉斯加 NORAD 地区发言人 Kitsana Dounglomchan 上尉在一封电子邮件中表示：“虽然飞机在 20 世纪 80 年代处于警戒状态是很常见的事情，但这次部署标志着数十年来飞机在厄尔克森首次处于警戒状态。”作为美加国土防御演习的一部分，谢米亚部署以远程行动结束。当 F-16 战机从厄尔克森起飞，覆盖阿拉斯加战区南部时，位于西边 1,600 英里的艾尔森空军基地的 F-35 和 F-16 战机也起飞，覆盖战区西北部。加拿大 CF-18 飞机从距谢米亚 2,600 英里的冷湖基地起飞，覆盖北部地区。
阿拉斯加北美防空司令部司令、空军中将罗伯特·戴维斯在一份新闻稿中表示，从厄尔克森出发的行动“证明我们可以部署到严峻的地点，保持警戒，在短时间内发射，并无缝整合美国和加拿大军队以保卫北方通道”。自二战以来，美国军方一直在谢米亚地区活跃。冷战期间，该基地驻有加油机和侦察机以及雷达，以监视苏联的活动，特别是苏联的洲际弹道导弹。大型 Cobra Dane 雷达建于 20 世纪 70 年代，至今仍用于监测导弹活动。最近在谢米亚的部署突显了其作为阿留申群岛栖息地的持续重要性，阿留申群岛横跨连接太平洋和北极的战略重要水域。 2024 年 9 月，美国士兵使用 HIMARS 发射器进行了一次“兵力投送行动”，此前俄罗斯和中国在该地区进行了一系列活动，其中包括中俄轰炸机在阿拉斯加附近进行的首次巡逻。最近的其他演习似乎侧重于保护该岛的基础设施免受海上入侵和空袭。据一份新闻稿称，在厄里克森期间，飞行员还认证了该基地的飞机拦截系统，可以处理 F-16 战斗机，“进一步验证了厄里克森机场作为未来战斗机在严峻机场执行任务的可行地点”。
Dounglomchan拒绝就厄尔克森的未来行动发表评论，但表示北美防空司令部保持着“作战能力”，可以“在我们选择的时间和地点”在阿拉斯加和北极周围调动部队，并且“经常到厄尔克森这样的偏远地区”。随着谢米亚演习的结束，空军分享了未来在太平洋中部岛屿上的行动计划。 在 10 月底发布的一份提案中，空军表示将研究每年在北马里亚纳群岛联邦罗塔岛、塞班岛和天宁岛的机场进行多达 1,500 次甚至可能超过 1,800 次飞机行动（例如起飞和降落）的影响。这些作业将是小型、中型和大型演习的一部分

【原文 English Original】
The U.S. Air Force is stepping up its training on the country’s westernmost islands as it seeks to develop more places from which to project power and monitor adversaries across the Pacific and the Arctic. Those efforts were visible in late October, when airmen deployed to Shemya Island in Alaska’s Aleutian Islands for a rare exercise, and when the Air Force released a proposal outlining its plans for operations on islands near Guam. On Shemya, which is closer to Russia than to mainland Alaska , F-16s, tankers and cargo planes deployed to Eareckson Air Station from Oct. 18 to Oct. 26. While there, the jets “sat alert,” with crews in position and maintaining readiness to launch on short notice. “While it was commonplace for aircraft to sit alert in the 1980s, this deployment marks the first time in decades that aircraft have sat alert at Eareckson,” Capt. Kitsana Dounglomchan, Alaskan NORAD Region spokesperson, said in an email. The Shemya deployment ended with long-range operations as part of a U.S.-Canada homeland-defense exercise. As F-16s launched from Eareckson to cover the southern portion of the Alaska theater of operations, F-35s and F-16s at Eielson Air Force Base 1,600 miles to the west took off to cover the northwest portion of the theater. Canadian CF-18s flew from their base at Cold Lake, 2,600 miles from Shemya, to cover the northern part. Operating from Eareckson “proved we can deploy to an austere location, maintain alert, launch on short notice, and seamlessly integrate U.S. and Canadian forces to defend the northern approaches,” Air Force Lt. Gen. Robert Davis, commander of the Alaskan NORAD region, said in a press release. The U.S. military has been active on Shemya since World War II. During the Cold War, the base hosted refueling and surveillance aircraft as well as radars to monitor Soviet activity, especially Soviet ICBMs. The massive Cobra Dane radar was built there in the 1970s and is still used to monitor missile activity. Recent deployments to Shemya underscore its continued relevance as a perch in the Aleutians, which stretch across strategically important waters linking the Pacific and Arctic. A “ force projection operation ” by U.S. soldiers with HIMARS launchers in September 2024 came after a flurry of Russian and Chinese activity in the area, including the first Sino-Russian bomber patrol near Alaska. Other recent exercises appear to have focused on defending the island’s infrastructure from seaborne incursions and aerial attacks. While at Eareckson, airmen also certified the base’s aircraft-arresting system to handle F-16s, “further validating Eareckson Air Station as a viable location for future fighter operations from an austere airfield,” according to a press release. Dounglomchan declined to comment on future operations at Eareckson but said NORAD maintains “the operational capability” to move forces around Alaska and the Arctic “at a time and place of our choosing” and “oftentimes to remote locations like Eareckson.” As the drills on Shemya wrapped up, the Air Force shared its plans for future operations on islands in the central Pacific. In a proposal released at the end of October, the service said it would study the impact of conducting up to 1,500 and potentially more than 1,800 aircraft operations, such as takeoffs and landings, annually at airfields on Rota, Saipan, and Tinian in the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. The operations would be part of small, medium and large drills held several times a year for a few weeks at a time. They would also involve deployment of up to 550,000 gallons of fuel and up to 1,000 personnel at each airfield, as well as munitions, temporary infrastructure, and support operations. The Air Force said its study would assess “the potential social, economic, and environmental effects” of those operations. HC-130J Combat King II pilots assigned to the 211th Rescue Squadron pilot an aircraft en route from Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson to Eareckson Air Station, Alaska, on Oct. 19, 2026. (Airman 1st Class Frank Houseton/U.S. Air Force) The study won’t be completed until mid-2028, but the proposal highlights the Air Force’s recent focus on those islands, especially Tinian, where airmen are refurbishing North Field , one of the U.S.’s largest and most important WWII airbases. North Field was abandoned and overgrown after the war, but airmen have been clearing vegetation, removing debris and rehabilitating runways since late 2023. That work is ongoing but had progressed enough by mid-2025 for North Field to be deemed “a semi-permanent [contingency] location” for the Air Force’s main base on Guam, about 100 miles to the south. The Northern Marianas is a U.S. territory in the Second Island Chain, which stretches from Japan through the central Pacific to Indonesia. The Air Force has been scouting airfields in that island chain and conducting renovations and upgrades to make them better able to support its Agile Combat Employment concept, which emphasizes dispersal and resilience to counter the threat from China. “China’s missile force is large, but it’s not unlimited. Every additional airfield from where the Air Force can operate is another of targets China has to cover. That’s the logic behind Agile Combat Employment,” said Kelly Greico, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center. Improvements on Shemya and in the Northern Marianas enhance the Air Force’s ability to operate in those places, but those operations are influenced by the islands’ locations, according to Greico, whose research focuses on airpower strategy. Shemya “is primarily about homeland defense. Its location in the North Pacific makes it useful mainly as a forward operating location for NORAD,” Greico said. “The value of the remote airfield lies less in its ability to generate sorties under contested conditions than in its geographic position in intercepting Russian aircraft forward.” But investments in Rota, Tinian, and Saipan, Greico added, “are primarily about expanding the number of locations from which the Air Force could operate, reducing its dependence on Andersen Air Base at Guam.” Both Shemya and the Northern Marianas provide the benefit of being U.S. territory, giving the Pentagon greater freedom to operate. Bases in the Philippines and Japan are closer to China, but those countries have more control over what U.S. forces do at their facilities and may limit their access and operations during a crisis or conflict. Geography tempers those political benefits, however. In the Stimson Center’s modeling , dispersal had “the biggest effect of any countermeasure we tested,” Greico said. “But the effect is much smaller in the Second Island Chain than in Japan, because there just aren’t many runways out there.” “Chinese missile strikes could keep U.S. runways in Guam and other Pacific islands closed to tankers and bombers for about four days. Adding civilian airfields in Guam, the Northern Marianas, and Palau only reduced those times by a matter of hours,” Greico added. “Geography matters here. There’s a lot of water out there, but not much land.”

title: Watchdog flags fraud, failed Pentagon audit as defense priorities
zh_title: 监管机构将欺诈和五角大楼审计失败列为国防优先事项
summary: 在五角大楼连续第九次审计失败后几天，其监督办公室将消除欺诈和实现廉洁财务审计列为国防部下一财年最紧迫的战略挑战。随着特朗普政府要求国会提供创纪录的 1.5 万亿美元用于国防，国防部监察长本周发布了一份年度报告，列出了国防部在执行国防战略时面临的七个主要障碍。根据该办公室的说法，优先事项（未按优先顺序排列）范围从
content:
在五角大楼连续第九次审计失败后几天，其监督办公室将消除欺诈和实现廉洁财务审计列为国防部下一财年最紧迫的战略挑战。随着特朗普政府要求国会提供创纪录的 1.5 万亿美元用于国防，国防部监察长本周发布了一份年度报告，列出了国防部在执行国防战略时面临的七个主要障碍。该办公室表示，优先事项（排名不分先后）包括从威慑中国到振兴国防工业基础，再到支持作战人员和财务透明度。 2026年国防战略将保卫“美国本土”和西半球置于对抗中国之上，并宣布了“特朗普门罗主义的推论”，优先考虑美国在西半球的主导地位以及美国进入巴拿马运河和墨西哥湾的机会。以下是监察长办公室确定的挑战。报告称，“考虑到国防部的广泛业务和庞大的预算，欺诈风险是固有的”，并强调五角大楼拥有最大的可自由支配的联邦预算，并要求国会将其当前资金增加 42%。赫格斯发起反对政府浪费的运动，并承诺消除五角大楼的裁员。
2025 年，在对自己的信号使用情况进行调查时，赫格斯发布了一份备忘录，讨论 IG 办公室的改革问题。他告诉军事领导人，该办公室的系统已经“武器化，让抱怨者、空想家和表现不佳的人坐上驾驶座”。实现干净的财务审计 2018 年，五角大楼首次审计失败后，国会给了国防部 10 年的时间（直到 2028 年 12 月 31 日）通过审计。尽管今年再次失败，但一位官员告诉路透社，审计发现五角大楼 25 个实体中有 14 个通过了财务报表，高于去年的 11 个。审计人员现在正在使用人工智能来处理和测试五角大楼许多过时系统的更多数据。该部门成立了联合审计工作组，该小组由文职人员、军人和私营部门专家组成，旨在解决持续存在的问题。确保有足够的能力保卫美国本土 国防战略将保卫“美国本土”和西半球放在首位。监察长发现部署到美国边境的部队面临压力，并表示目前正在调查国内国民警卫队部署的有效性。该报告还指出了基础设施网络安全和重要设施周围的反无人机能力方面的差距。确保有足够的能力威慑中国 排在第二位的是美国
正在通过在太平洋群岛第一岛链建立强大的态势来重点关注印度-太平洋地区的威慑。监察长发现了“前沿驻扎后勤网络的准备情况、预置设备的条件和可用性、有争议的海上保障路线的弹性以及国防部从美国太平洋司令部责任区多个地点分散和操作空中力量的能力”等问题。  各军种已开始为面向太平洋的战斗做准备。例如，陆军正在加速开发下一代突击倾转旋翼机“Che”

【原文 English Original】
Days after the Pentagon failed its ninth consecutive audit, its oversight office ranked eliminating fraud and achieving a clean financial audit among the Defense Department’s most pressing strategic challenges for the upcoming fiscal year.  As the Trump administration asks Congress for a record $1.5 trillion for national defense, the Department of Defense Inspector General this week released an annual report listing the seven top hurdles facing the department as it executes the National Defense Strategy. The priorities — not ranked in order of priority, according to the office — range from deterring China to energizing the defense-industrial base to supporting warfighters and financial transparency.  The 2026 National Defense Strategy elevated defense of the “U.S. Homeland” and the Western Hemisphere above countering China and declared the “Trump Corollary to the Monroe Doctrine,” prioritizing American dominance in the hemisphere and American access to the Panama Canal and Gulf of Mexico.  Here are the challenges identified by the IG’s office. Eliminating fraud “Considering the Department’s extensive operations and sizeable budget, the risk of fraud is inherent,” the report said, emphasizing that the Pentagon has the largest discretionary federal budget and is asking Congress for a 42% increase in its current funding. Hegseth has campaigned against government waste and pledged to eliminate redundancy in the Pentagon. In 2025, amid an investigation into his own Signal use, Hegseth issued a memo addressing reforms to the IG office. He told military leaders that the office’s systems had been “weaponized, putting complainers, ideologues and poor performers in the driver’s seat.” Achieving a clean financial audit In 2018, after the Pentagon failed its first-ever audit, Congress gave the Defense Department 10 years — until Dec. 31, 2028 — to pass. Though it failed again this year, an official told Reuters that the audit found 14 of 25 Pentagon entities’ passing financial statements, up from 11 the prior year. Auditors are now using artificial intelligence to process and test more data on many of the Pentagon’s outdated systems. The department established Joint Task Force-Audit, which is a group of civilians, service members and private sector experts to address continued issues.  Ensuring sufficient capacity to defend the U.S. homeland The National Defense Strategy places defense of the “U.S. homeland” and Western Hemisphere in the top slot. The IG identified strain on forces deployed to the U.S. border and said it is currently investigating the effectiveness of domestic National Guard deployments. The report also flagged gaps in infrastructure cybersecurity and in counter-unmanned aerial capabilities around important installations.  Ensuring sufficient capacity to deter China Bumped to second priority, the U.S. is focusing on deterrence in the Indo-Pacific by building a strong posture in the First Island Chain, a set of Pacific archipelagos.  The IG identified issues “with the readiness of forward-stationed logistics networks, condition and availability of prepositioned equipment, resilience of contested maritime sustainment routes, and the Department’s ability to disperse and operate airpower from multiple locations in the U.S. Pacific Command area of responsibility.”  The services have begun to prepare for a Pacific-oriented fight. For instance, the Army is accelerating development of its next-generation assault tiltrotor aircraft, the Cheyenne II , designed for use in a Pacific theater.  Increasing burden-sharing with U.S. allies and partners Burden sharing has become a signature phrase for the Trump administration, from discussions about rotational forces in Europe to counterterrorism operations in Africa to deterrence in the Indo-Pacific. The office “identified lessons learned from 10 years of reports related to burden sharing with international partners, noting lack of proper reimbursement by international partners for supplies and services provided by the Department,” the report said. It did not provide specific examples or list the international partners in question. Supercharging the U.S. defense industrial base while ensuring accountability The report said the IG continues to find production shortfalls and, in some cases, a lack of accountability for major defense contractors that fall short of requirements. The Defense Department “is sometimes so dependent on certain contractors that it continues to give them funds even when they fail to deliver or delay delivery by years,” the report said. Additionally, the agency said contractors had not delivered the agreed-upon amount of munitions on time, leading to diminished stockpiles of critical munitions. Earlier this year, the agency also found that the Pentagon’s drive to get weapons faster bypassed acquisition steps meant to ensure new systems work before reaching the force. Supporting the warfighter and their family The new report flagged issues with overseas medical care — including patient safety — the health of trainees, housing quality and issues in the review process for child abuse accusations at childcare centers. According to a new Pentagon directive , all military services must now resolve emergency living conditions within 24 hours or relocate the service member.
